title: Seeds: eudicot and monocot
caption: A seed has a testa, an embryo (radicle and plumule) and a food store. A eudicot seed such as a bean has two cotyledons, which hold the food; a monocot seed such as maize has one cotyledon and stores food in the endosperm. The micropyle is where the pollen tube entered; water enters there at germination.
alt: Two seeds side by side. A bean has a thick testa round two large cotyledons, with a plumule at the top and a radicle at the bottom. A maize grain has a testa round a large food store, the endosperm, with a single small cotyledon, plumule and radicle at one side.
description: The embryo is the radicle (young root) and plumule (young shoot) on the cotyledon(s).
Eudicot: two cotyledons that store food.
Monocot: one cotyledon; food stored in the endosperm.
